t: Feria Secunda infra Hebdomadam XV post Octavam Pentecostes V. Augusti ~ IV. classis
Commemoratio  ad Laudes tantum: Ss. Felicis et Adaucti Martyrum
tv: Feria Secunda infra Hebdomadam XV post Octavam Pentecostes V. Augusti ~ IV. classis

b.5e45cdb0ec:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Ecclesiástici
<r>Sir 7:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> Noli fácere mala, et non te apprehéndent:
<n>2</n> Discéde ab iníquo, et defícient mala abs te.
<n>3</n> Fili, non sémines mala in sulcis iniustítiæ et non metes ea in séptuplum.
<n>4</n> Noli quǽrere a dómino ducátum, neque a rege cáthedram honóris.
<n>5</n> Non te iustífices ante Deum, quóniam ágnitor cordis ipse est: et penes regem noli velle vidéri sápiens.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> In princípio Deus ántequam terram fáceret, priúsquam abýssos constitúeret, priúsquam prodúceret fontes aquárum, antequam montes collocaréntur,
* Ante omnes colles generávit me Dóminus.
<r>℣.</r> Quando præparábat cælos, áderam, cum eo cuncta compónens.
<r>℟.</r> Ante omnes colles generávit me Dóminus.
b.410b270c05:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Ecclesiasticus
<r>Sir 7:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> Do no evils, and no evils shall lay hold of thee.
<n>2</n> Depart from the unjust, and evils shall depart from thee.
<n>3</n> My son, sow not evils in the furrows of injustice, and thou shalt not reap them sevenfold.
<n>4</n> Seek not of the Lord a pre-eminence, nor of the king the seat of honour.
<n>5</n> Justify not thyself before God, for he knoweth the heart: and desire not to appear wise before the king.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> God possessed me in the beginning, before He made the earth, before He created the depths, before He caused the fountains of water to spring.before the mountains were settled, before there were any hills, did the Lord beget me.
<r>℣.</r> When He prepared the heavens, I was there with Him, ordering all things.
* Before the mountains were settled, before there were any hills, did the Lord beget me.
b.54c63e1560:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad gáudia paradísi perdúcat nos misericórdia Christi.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Sir 7:6-10</r>
<n>6</n> Noli quǽrere fíeri iudex, nisi váleas virtúte irrúmpere iniquitátes; ne forte extiméscas fáciem poténtis et ponas scándalum in æquitáte tua.
<n>7</n> Non pecces in multitúdinem civitátis nec te immíttas in pópulum:
<n>8</n> Neque álliges duplícia peccáta, nec enim in uno eris immúnis.
<n>9</n> Noli esse pusillánimis in ánimo tuo,
<n>10</n> Exoráre et fácere eleemósynam ne despícias.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Gyrum cæli circuívi sola, et in flúctibus maris ambulávi, in omni gente et in omni pópulo primátum ténui:
* Superbórum et sublímium colla própria virtúte calcávi.
<r>℣.</r> Ego in altíssimis hábito, et thronus meus in colúmna nubis.
<r>℟.</r> Superbórum et sublímium colla própria virtúte calcávi.
b.e0e7f38fb2:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Sir 7:6-10</r>
<n>6</n> Seek not to be made a judge, unless thou have strength enough to extirpate iniquities: lest thou fear the person of the powerful, and lay a stumblingblock for thy integrity.
<n>7</n> Offend not against the multitude of a city, neither cast thyself in upon the people,
<n>8</n> Nor bind sin to sin: for even in one thou shalt not be unpunished.
<n>9</n> Be not fainthearted in thy mind:
<n>10</n> Neglect not to pray, and to give alms.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked on the waves of the sea. In every nation and in every people, I held the first place.
* In the greatness of my strength have I trodden under my feet the necks of such as be haughty and proud.
<r>℣.</r> I dwell in the highest places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
<r>℟.</r> In the greatness of my strength have I trodden under my feet the necks of such as be haughty and proud.
b.1ba535267f:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>Sir 7:11-15</r>
<n>11</n> Ne dicas: In multitúdine múnerum meórum respíciet Deus et, offerénte me Deo altíssimo, múnera mea suscípiet.
<n>12</n> Non irrídeas hóminem in amaritúdine ánimæ; est enim qui humíliat et exáltat, circumspéctor Deus.
<n>13</n> Noli aráre mendácium advérsus fratrem tuum, neque in amícum simíliter fácias.
<n>14</n> Noli velle mentíri omne mendácium; assidúitas enim illíus non est bona.
<n>15</n> Noli verbósus esse in multitúdine presbyterórum, et non íteres verbum in oratióne tua.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Emítte, Dómine, sapiéntiam de sede magnitúdinis tuæ, ut mecum sit et mecum labóret:
* Ut sciam, quid accéptum sit coram te omni témpore.
<r>℣.</r> Da mihi, Dómine, sédium tuárum assistrícem sapiéntiam.
<r>℟.</r> Ut sciam quid accéptum sit coram te omni témpore.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Omni témpore.
b.0e63ebd80e:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>Sir 7:11-15</r>
<n>11</n> Say not: God will have respect to the multitude of my gifts, and when I offer to the most high God, he will accept my offerings.
<n>12</n> Laugh no man to scorn in the bitterness of his soul: for there is one that humbleth and exalteth, God who seeth all.
<n>13</n> Devise not a lie against thy brother: neither do the like against thy friend.
<n>14</n> Be not willing to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.
<n>15</n> Be not full of words in a multitude of ancients, and repeat not the word in thy prayer.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> O send out wisdom from the throne of thy glory, O Lord, to be with me, and to labour with me,
* That I may know at all times what is pleasing unto thee.
<r>℣.</r> Give me wisdom, O Lord, that sitteth by thy throne.
<r>℟.</r> That I may know at all times what is pleasing unto thee.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
* That I may know at all times what is pleasing unto thee.
b.da07ae45fd:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>E</c>cclésiam tuam, Dómine, miserátio continuáta mundet et múniat: et quia sine te non potest salva consístere; tuo semper múnere gubernétur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.d9840fc3e0:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we beseech thee, let thy continual pity cleanse and defend thy Church, and because it cannot continue in safety without thy succour, preserve it evermore by thy help and goodness.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio Ss. Felicis et Adaucti Martyrum</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Isti sunt Sancti, qui pro Dei amóre minas hóminum contempsérunt: sancti Mártyres in regno cælórum exsúltant cum Angelis. O quam pretiósa est mors Sanctórum, qui assídue assístunt ante Dóminum, et ab ínvicem non sunt separáti!

<r>℣.</r> Mirábilis Deus.
<r>℟.</r> In sanctis suis.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>M</c>aiestátem tuam, Dómine, súpplices exorámus: ut, sicut nos iúgiter Sanctórum tuórum commemoratióne lætíficas; ita semper supplicatióne deféndas.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of St. Felix and Adauctus, Martyrs</r>
<r>Ant.</r> These are the holy ones who for the love of Christ, recked nothing of the threats of men. In the kingdom of heaven the holy martyrs are filled with joy in the company of Angels. O how precious in the sight of the Lord was the death of these His saints who now stand day and night in His presence and are not divided the one from the other.

<r>℣.</r> Mirábilis Deus.
<r>℟.</r> In sanctis suis.

b.5c57170bb3:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>P</c>rídie Kaléndas Septémbris Luna vicésima nona. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>ancti Raymúndi Nonnáti, ex Ordine beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum, Cardinális et Confessóris; cuius dies natális séptimo Kaléndas Septémbris recólitur.
<h>A</h>pud montem Senárium, in Etrúria, natális sancti Bonaiúnctæ Confessóris, e septem Fundatóribus Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis; qui, de Passióne Domínica ad fratres verba fáciens, in manus Dómini trádidit spíritum. Ipsíus autem ac Sociórum festum prídie Idus Februárii celebrátur.
<h>T</h>réviris item natális sancti Paulíni Epíscopi, qui, témpore Ariánæ infestatiónis, ab Ariáno Imperatóre Constántio ob cathólicam fidem relegátus exsílio, et extra Christiánum nomen usque ad mortem mutándo exsília fatigátus, tandem, apud Phrýgiam defúnctus, beátæ passiónis corónam percépit a Dómino.
<h>T</h>ránsaquis, ad lacum Fúcinum, in Marsis, natális quoque sanctórum Mártyrum Cæsídii Presbýteri, et Sociórum; qui martýrio coronáti sunt in persecutióne Maximíni.
<h>I</h>tem sanctórum Mártyrum Robustiáni et Marci.
<h>C</h>æsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sanctórum Theódoti, Rufínæ et Ammiæ; quorum duo primi paréntes fuérunt sancti Mamántis Mártyris, quem Rufína in cárcere péperit, et Ammia educávit.
<h>A</h>ntisiodóri sancti Optáti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>I</h>n Anglia sancti Aidáni, Epíscopi Lindisfarnénsis; cuius ánimam, cum sanctus Cuthbértus, cuius memória tertiodécimo Kaléndas Aprílis cólitur, tunc óvium pastor, in cælum ferri vidísset, relíctis óvibus, factus est Mónachus.
<h>A</h>pud Nuscum sancti Amáti Epíscopi.
<h>A</h>thénis sancti Aristídis, fide et sapiéntia claríssimi, qui Hadriáno Príncipi egrégium de religióne Christiána volúmen óbtulit, nostri dogmátis cóntinens ratiónem; et quod Christus Iesus solus esset Deus, præsénte ipso Imperatóre, luculentíssime perorávit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.2df6e2343c:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>ugust 31st 2027, the 29th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Cardinal Raymond, surnamed the Unborn, of the Order of Blessed Mary of Ransom for the Redemption of Prisoners, a man famous for the holiness of his life and for his wonderful works, of whom mention is made upon the 26th day of this present month of August.
<h>U</h>pon the same 31st day of August, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Monte Senario, hard by Florence, [in the year 1257,] the blessed Confessor Bonajuncta [Manetti,] one of the Seven Founders of the Order of Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who gave up the ghost into the Lord's hands as he was discoursing to his brethren concerning the same Lord's Passion.
<h>A</h>t Trier, [in the year 358,] holy Paulinus, Bishop [of that see.] In the time of the persecution under the Arians he was exiled by Constantius the Arian Emperor on account of his Catholic belief, and when he had been wearied out by changing the places of his exile, even beyond the bounds of Christendom, he at length died in Phrygia, and received a crown from the Lord in reward of his blessed sufferings.
<h>A</h>t Trasacco, on the Lake of Celano, the holy martyrs Caesidius the Priest and his Companions, who were crowned with martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Maximin.
<h>L</h>ikewise the holy martyrs Robustian and Mark.
<h>A</h>t Cassarea, in Cappadocia, [in the third century,] holy Theodotus, Rufina, and Ammia. Theodotus and Rufina were the father and mother of the holy martyr Mamas. Rufina gave him birth in prison, and Ammia was his nurse.
<h>A</h>t Auxerre, [in the sixth century,] the holy Confessor Optatus, Bishop [of that see.]
<h>I</h>n England, [in the year 651,] holy Aidan, Bishop of Lindisfarne. Holy Cuthbert, who was then a shepherd lad, saw the soul of Aidan carried up into heaven, and he thereupon left his sheep and became a monk.
<h>A</h>t Nusco, [in the year 1093,] holy Amatus, Bishop [of that see.]
<h>A</h>t Athens, [in the second century,] the holy Aristides, a man illustrious for his faith and wisdom, who offered to the Emperor Hadrian a book upon the Christian religion, containing an exposition of our doctrine, and delivered a most able discourse in the presence of the said Emperor, to prove that Christ Jesus is the only God.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
